title: Codegen options (Agent 9): A = devoff2-bin (S2 sources, S1 codegen) vs B = devoffB-bin (the same S2 sources + the batch codegen config). Title/attract loop, no input needed. Superseded for the user timing window by matrix-window4.json (B vs devoff2)
notes: Spec: perf-notes/agent9-codegen.md, 'Run spec for the codegen-options timing run'. B = build/agent2/devoffB-bin (Agent 2 stages it after the B build; a missing bin skips the arm). A = build/agent2/devoff2-bin, so the codegen options are the only difference.

Run matrix-codegen-check.json first: the functional gate (B boots and plays Agent 10's route with no REX_FATAL, __builtin_trap, 'Switch case out of range', hang or crash, and no new ERROR/WARN lines against A) and one profile run of each build. Do not time B if the gate failed.

Order: roundrobin gives a b | b a | a b | b a (Agent 9 asks for alternating A/B, at least 3 each). One unscored cold run per bin comes first, because B is a new exe on its first launch (driver and file caches).

Metrics (Agent 9): frame time p50/p99 per run (p95: compute from perf.csv), cpu_cores (process CPU; under the 60 fps cap a codegen win shows here rather than in the median) and the first-frame time (boot). Main-thread CPU per frame is not measured by the runner; the check matrix's profile runs give per-thread samples and the top guest functions.
Same scene, settings and window state as the other OFF matrices: the title/attract loop, the harness toml (framerate_limit = 60), audio muted, profiler off.
